item.dc:creator: MT newswire
item.content:encoded: 03:39 PM EDT, 09/18/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Financial stocks were mixed in late Friday afternoon trading, with the NYSE Financial Index declining 0.5% and the State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) fractionally higher. The Philadelphia Housing Index dropped 1.3%, and the State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) shed 0.7%. Bitcoin (BTC-USD) rose 5.9% to $81,042, and the yield on 10-year US Treasuries gained 5.7 basis points to 5%. In corporate news, Blackstone (BX) has secured a loan to help fund its acquisition of a controlling stake in data center cooling firm Flow Control from Audax Private Equity, Bloomberg reported. UBS (UBS) has been tasked with providing the loan, the report said, adding that the loan is expected to launch in the coming weeks. Blackstone shares were down 0.4%, and UBS was 0.1% higher.

item.dc:creator: MT newswire
item.content:encoded: 03:34 PM EDT, 09/18/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Energy stocks fell late Friday afternoon with the NYSE Energy Sector Index declining 0.7% and the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE) dropping 0.4%. The Philadelphia Oil Service Sector Index fell 0.8%, and the Dow Jones US Utilities Index dropped 1.1%. West Texas Intermediate crude oil fell 2% to $99.90 a barrel, and global benchmark Brent shed 1.6% to $103.18 a barrel. Henry Hub natural gas futures eased 0.1% to $2.90 per 1 million BTU. In corporate news, Westinghouse Electric is aiming for a valuation of over $50 billion in its US initial public offering, Bloomberg reported. The company, which provides reactor technology to nuclear power plants and is co-owned by Brookfield Renewable Partners (BEP) and Cameco (CCJ), is looking to file publicly as early as October, the report said. Brookfield Renewable shares rose 0.9%, and Cameco fell 1%.

item.title: Market Chatter: Stellantis, Unifor Should Resume Talks, Canadian Industry Minister Says
item.description: 03:12 PM EDT, 09/18/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Stellantis (STLA) and its unionized Canadian workers should resume labor talks, Bloomberg reported Friday, citing
item.dc:creator: MT newswire
item.content:encoded: 03:12 PM EDT, 09/18/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Stellantis (STLA) and its unionized Canadian workers should resume labor talks, Bloomberg reported Friday, citing Canadian Industry Minister Melanie Joly. Joly told reporters in Ottawa the two sides need to return to the table, calling the government a trustworthy partner in reaching a deal, the report said. A collective agreement between Stellantis and Unifor, representing about 9,000 workers, expires Sunday, with strike action remaining a possibility, according to Unifor President Lana Payne, the report added. Joly said the government did not participate in talks between Stellantis and Roshel, which is seeking to buy an idled Stellantis plant near Toronto, and reiterated the plant must reopen or the government will seek repayment of prior financial assistance, Bloomberg reported. Stellantis did not immediately respond to a request for comment from MT Newswires. (Market Chatter news is derived from conversations with market professionals globally. This information is believed to be from reliable sources but may include rumor and speculation. Accuracy is not guaranteed.) Price: 4.83, Change: -0.23, Percent Change: -4.46
